correctness.rationale: For Z_j=1+nu_2(j), adjacent valuations differ, so even-length palindromes cannot occur. Every odd palindrome centered at m has radius strictly below 2^{nu_2(m)}, and every such interval is a palindrome; the claimed boundary obstruction follows by comparing valuations at the next radius. The corresponding endpoints a<b differ in exactly one bit after binary-reflected Gray transform G(x)=x xor floor(x/2). Thus any partition of the prefix induces an increasing integer Gray-hypercube path. A geodesic has precisely popcount(G(n)) flips, and the explicit backwards highest-bit step m=2^{k+1}-1-n constructs one. For an optimal cut path, selected Gray flip k is legal iff the number of previously selected larger positions is even. Deleting the last position proves f(r)=ceil(r/2)f(r-1), f(0)=1, hence f(r)=ceil(r/2)!floor(r/2)!. No index n>0 is omitted. A genuinely independent reversal-based DP, not Gray-edge recognition, checks every length 0..150 with exact integer multiplicities; it is corroboration, not the infinite proof.
